speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history suggestive of bone fragility. To narrow this down, have you experienced any fractures from minimal trauma, or perhaps noticed excessive joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of delayed menarche, clitoromegaly, and severe acne is concerning for an androgen-excess disorder like Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH). Given your history of fractures from minimal trauma, have you been diagnosed with or tested for osteoporosis or low bone density? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrolytes, 17-Hydroxyprogesterone, Bone_Density_Scan.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) with secondary osteoporosis. The clinical triad of ambiguous genitalia (labial fusion, clitoromegaly) at birth, severe acne, and delayed menarche indicates lifelong androgen excess due to enzyme deficiency; the fractures confirm significant bone density loss likely secondary to chronic glucocorticoid therapy or the underlying endocrine disorder.
